items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: I was at Atlantic Records one day I think working on an Aretha Franklin record.

ctx.x: I was at Atlantic Records one day I think working on an Aretha Franklin record. And Atlanta has a main studio and then they have like a mixing room studio. And Dr. John was in the mixing room with I think – I forgot who was producing it, either Arif Mardin was working or Joel Dorn. One of those producers. I was working with both of them a lot of the time. So I was on my way to a jingle date, it was like 1:30, and I had to go to a 2:00 jingle date. I’d just finished a 10-1 at Atlantic. I’m at the elevator with my…

doing? You got a minute?” I said, “Yeah, what’s up?” He said, “Man we forgot to put a sax solo on this tune. Can you come and play a little solo for me?” I said, “Okay.” So I go in the mix room. There’s a little amp in the corner, a little Fender thank God in the corner, mics it up, because it wasn’t really a studio, it was just a little, you know we’re in a studio, a little mixing room. So he said, “It’s in E flat.” And they rolled right to the place where I’m going to solo so I don’t hear the song. There’s like…
